newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Goodman to wield collective power - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Goodman to wield collective power - CEO.

text.p: Australasian food group Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Friday it would focus on wielding its collective power in dealing with customers rather than presenting itself as a series smaller units as it had done in the past.

"We're not making use of the great asset we've got. One of the things that distinguishes us from other local food suppliers is that we are very big, very important," chief executive David Hearn told a briefing of journalists.

"Our relative fighting weight versus our customers' isn't as high as it should be. Go in as Goodman Fielder -- we're the largest food supplier in Australasia -- now let's sit down as two equals," he said.

Hearn said the issue for the moment was to aggregate Goodman's "power" with its suppliers on the one side, and its customers on the other, but the change of focus could eventually see the company market its various products under the Goodman Fielder brand name.
"That may or may not come later," he said.
On Thursday Goodman reported an annual net profit of A$28.3 million, up from a loss of A$52.8 million for the previous year.
Hearn said trading conditions were "very tough", but he was confident the company would improve profit in the current year.
He said Goodman did not anticipate making any significant acquisitions in the current year.
"We're concentrating on getting our current businesses up and running and doing well," he said.
